JUDGMENT BRIEF STATEMENT OF REASONS FOR DECISION OF THE CASE 1.
The present case has been instituted on the basis of charge-sheet filed against the accused Afzal for the offences punishable under Sections 287/337/506 IPC, who is stated to be on bail.

2. In brief, the facts of the case as per the prosecution are that on 06.03.2019, victim Dilshad was admitted to Dr. Hedgewar Hospital with burn injuries from a gas stove/fire incident at Bharat Chicken, Karkardooma.

He stated that he was heating the chulha for preparing chicken rolls when the gas leaked and caught fire and the manager Mukhtar had been informed earlier about the leakage but no safety measures were taken.
No owner/manager accompanied him to the hospital.
MLC and statements confirmed injuries due to negligent handling of gas equipment.
Police seized the gas cylinder and chulha.
Owner Afjal later produced his trade and food safety licences.
After investigation, chargesheet under Sections 286/337/506 IPC was filed for negligence and unsafe conditions at the shop.

3. Upon filing of the charge-sheet, Ld. Predecessor Court vide order dated MANISH JAIN page No.

Anand Vihar 09.06.2023 took the cognizance of the offences against accused.
Upon appearance of accused, copy of chargesheet was supplied to the accused and he was admitted to bail.
4. Thereafter, charge was framed vide order dated 27.02.2024 against accused for the offences punishable u/s 287/337/506 IPC to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

Thereafter,
the matter was put up for prosecution evidence.

5. Prosecution has examined PW-1 Dilshad, who is the complainant in this case, who deposed that on 06.03.2019, he was working as a chef at the shop of the accused Afzal which was his first day of work.
He was preparing chicken rolls at the shop situated near Karkardooma Metro Station.
At about 04:00 PM, while he attempted to light the gas stove using a matchstick, the stove caught fire and he sustained burn injuries on his face.

He stated that thereafter he called his uncle, Md. Nasim,
who reached the spot around 04:30 PM, after which he became unconscious.
PW-1 deposed that he can identify the accused however, the identity of accused remained undisputed by the defence.
He further stated that he had not given any statement to the police officials.
Since the witness was not disclosing the complete facts, Ld. APP was permitted to put leading questions.
On being confronted with his statement Ex. PW1/A, the witness denied having made such a statement to the police.

9. Perusal of the record reveals that the sole material witness of the prosecution, namely the complainant Dilshad, has turned hostile and has not supported the case of the prosecution.
The accused has been charged under Sections 287/337/506 IPC and the incident in question could have been proved only through the testimony of the complainant.
The remaining witnesses cited by the prosecution are merely formal in nature.
In these circumstances, the examination of the remaining formal witnesses would be a futile exercise and would not advance the case of the prosecution in any manner.
Accordingly, the remaining witnesses mentioned in the list of witnesses were dropped and PE stands closed.
10.As nothing incriminating has come on record against accused, recording of statement of accused u/s 313 Cr.P.C. is hereby dispensed with.

11.It is argued by Ld. Counsel for accused that since the complainant did not support the case of prosecution for the allegations so leveled against the accused, accused may be acquitted for the offences he is charged for.
12.On the other hand, Ld. APP for the State argued that since other witnesses are material witnesses, they be summoned and examined to prove the case of the prosecution.

I have heard the arguments and perused the case file.

14.It is the case of the prosecution that on 06.03.2019, the accused negligently failed to maintain the gas chulha under his control resulting in gas leakage due to which the complainant Dilshad sustained simple burn injuries while lighting it.
It is further alleged that the accused also threatened to kill the complainant.
Thus, to establish the offences under Sections 337/287/506 IPC, the testimony of complainant Dilshad, being the victim of the incident, was crucial.

15. Further, perusal of record reveals that all other witnesses were formal in nature, since from perusal of statement u/s 161 Cr.PC of other witnesses, it was revealed that none of the said witness was present at the alleged point of time at the spot who has seen the alleged offence.
PW-2 Naseem is also a formal witness as his testimony is entirely hearsay as he admittedly did not witness the incident himself.
He denied having any knowledge about the occurrence, denied giving any statement to police, and even failed to identify the accused.

Since the sole eye witness failed to identify the accused in the court as the perpetrator of the crime, the remaining witnesses being formal in nature were dropped from the list of witnesses and prosecution evidence was closed.

16.Considering that the complainant did not support the case of the prosecution and further failed to identify accused in the court and there is MANISH JAIN page No. 7 of 8 JAIN Date:
2025.11.18 16:11:10 +0530 (Manish Jain) ACJM:Shahdara:KKD:Delhi State Vs. Afzal FIR No.: 86/2019 PS:
Anand Vihar no other witness of prosecution who could have identified accused as perpetrator of crime, statement of the accused u/s 313 Cr.PC was dispensed with.

Reference can be made to the observations made by Hon'ble Apex Court in Satish Mehra v. Delhi Administration, reported as 1996 JCC 507, "in case where there is no prospect of the case ending in conviction, the valuable time of the court should not be wasted for holding a trial only for the purpose of formally completing the procedure to pronounce the conclusion on the future date."
17.In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, it is held that no incriminating evidence has come on record against for the offences u/s 287/337/506 IPC.
